findings.text: follow-on: the tests field claims `uv lock` -> EXIT=0 with "Added imas-alambic (dynamic)", but the log it cites in test_logs (runs/.../logs/uv-lock-scratch.log) contains EXIT=1 -- a hatchling build failure (OSError: Readme file does not exist: README.md) from the first scratch attempt before README.md was added. The successful EXIT=0 log exists only at /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../alambic-lock-scratch/uv-lock-scratch.log (node-local scratch, not cited, dies with the allocation), so the cited receipt is red while the recorded claim is green.

follow-on: the done-when says "uv lock, run in this worktree only", but uv lock/uv lock --check cannot run in the worktree: the .reckon-worktrees container is mounted read-only and pyproject's tool.uv.sources reach ../nova and ../imas-ink, which resolve into that read-only container. The measure ran in a $TMPDIR scratch mirror instead. Disclosed in evidence_inputs and compensated -- the scratch pyproject.toml is byte-identical to the worktree head and the 15 packages/imas-alambic files match, the lock records no absolute paths (grep -c /home = 0), and this review reproduced the check EXIT=0 -- but the literal done-when clause is unmet.

follow-on: the before/after name/version comparison cited by the manifest is against before.json, a 233-package snapshot that omits the four editable workspace packages present in the real base lock (imas-ambix, imas-ink, nova-cocos, nova-stella; base lock has 237). The claim still holds when checked against the actual base lock f78cad45:uv.lock -- imas-alambic added, 237->238 packages, zero version changes -- so the conclusion is right but the cited comparison base is not the base revision's lock.

item_verdicts.diff: read at ea4c205e against f78cad45; uv.lock gains the [manifest] members block, the imas-alambic editable package with its requires-dist, imas-alambic in imas-ambix's dependencies and its editable source entry; the evidence fragment records the lock regeneration. No source or test code changes.
item_verdicts.done_when: the fence asks uv lock to rewrite uv.lock in this worktree, uv lock --check to exit 0 at the head, the commit to touch uv.lock and the evidence fragment only, a before/after name/version comparison showing imas-alambic added with no other version changed, and no uv sync / plain uv run; the commit touches exactly those two paths and the comparison holds against the base lock, uv lock --check exits 0 (reproduced by this review in the scratch mirror), but the run could not execute uv lock in the worktree itself -- the read-only container mount blocks the ../nova and ../imas-ink path sources -- so the measure ran in a scratch mirror.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to regenerate imas-ambix uv.lock so it resolves the packages/imas-alambic workspace member added at f78cad45; commit ea4c205e adds the [manifest] members block (imas-alambic, imas-ambix) and the imas-alambic editable package entry to uv.lock, and adds imas-alambic to imas-ambix's dependencies -- exactly the deliverable.
item_verdicts.lock_validity: parsed uv.lock at head: 238 packages, changed_versions [] against f78cad45:uv.lock, added ['imas-alambic'], no absolute/scratch paths present; the committed lock is byte-identical to the scratch resolution, and this review ran `uv lock --check` in a faithful scratch mirror of the head (pyproject.toml identical, 15 packages/imas-alambic files identical) which resolved 238 packages and exited 0.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records commit ea4c205e8f481ce58cadd8de10e93a57f1662258, changed_paths uv.lock and the evidence fragment, states no blockers on the deliverable, and carries a correct follow_ons note that worktrees of this repo cannot run uv commands that resolve the path sources; its test_logs path for uv-lock-scratch.log points at a red (EXIT=1) log while the tests field claims EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the fence lists uv.lock, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-alambic-lock.html and docs/figures/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-alambic-lock; `git diff --stat f78cad45 ea4c205e` touches uv.lock (+30) and the evidence fragment (+20) only, so the diff is inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: the resolved lock is committed and is the durable deliverable, and it records no absolute paths so it is location-independent; the evidence supporting it is weaker -- the green gate log lives only in /tmp node-local scratch (gone when the allocation ends) and the run's own logs directory holds the red attempt -- so a later reader cannot reconcile the manifest's EXIT=0 claim from the cited path alone.
justifications.evidence: the artifact is independently verifiable and correct (name/version diff against the base lock shows imas-alambic added and zero version changes; this review reproduced uv lock --check EXIT=0 in a byte-faithful scratch mirror), but the manifest's cited uv-lock-scratch.log is the failed first attempt (EXIT=1, missing README.md) while the successful EXIT=0 log survives only in node-local scratch and is uncited, and the cited before.json omits the four editable packages the base lock carries.
justifications.fit: the change follows uv's own workspace idiom -- regenerate the lock rather than hand-edit it -- and matches plan jt60sa-facility-mint §2's requirement that ambix and imas-alambic share one lock and one version owner; it introduces no code and no new surface.
justifications.goal_fidelity: uv.lock at ea4c205e resolves the packages/imas-alambic workspace member: the [manifest] members block lists imas-alambic and imas-ambix, the imas-alambic editable entry carries the engine's six declared deps, and imas-ambix depends on imas-alambic -- the goal's deliverable verbatim.
justifications.reuse: the node reused `uv lock` to derive the resolution rather than editing uv.lock by hand, so the lock stays a generated artifact consistent with pyproject.toml and the workspace manifest; no duplication introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat f78cad45 ea4c205e touches only uv.lock and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-alambic-lock.html, both named in the node's write_paths; no source, test or other plan file was modified.
